::: {.lead}
Today you look inside the Office apps like in a lab. Each experiment has
two parts. **Part A** is in Word on the lab computer. **Part B** is on a
simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the
screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its box. At
the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word and File Explorer.
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Word (or Word on the web at
  `office.com`).
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · Three apps and their files

**The idea:** **Word** makes a **document**: pages of text, tables and
pictures. **Excel** makes a **workbook** with **worksheets**; one box of a
worksheet is a **cell**, and its name is the column and the row: **B3**.
**PowerPoint** makes a **presentation** with **slides**. All three have a
**title bar** (the file name), the ribbon and a **status bar** (page
number, zoom). **File → New** shows **templates**: ready-made files with a
design.

**Aim:** read the parts of an Office window, and start from a template.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Open `notice-start.docx` in Word (click **Enable Editing** if you see it).
   Read the title bar at the top and the status bar at the bottom.

   {{< record "Title bar … ; status bar: Page … of … ; … words" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The title bar shows **notice-start** (some computers also show
   `.docx`). The status bar shows **Page 1 of 1** and **59 words**. A Word
   file is a document: pages of text.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="59" unit="words" hint="Look at the left end of the status bar, at the bottom of the window."}
   How many words does the status bar show for the notice?

   Why: The status bar shows Page 1 of 1 and 59 words. A Word file is a document: pages of text.
   :::

2. In Word, click **File › New**, search for *invitation* and open one
   template (or any template that you see).

   {{< record "The name of my template" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good answer: the name of the template, for example "Event invitation".
   A template is a ready-made file with a design: you change only the text.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   What is a template?

   - [x] a ready-made file with a design: you change only the text

     Why: You start from the template and add your own content.

   - [ ] an empty document

     Why: A template already has a design and a layout.

   - [ ] a PDF copy of a document

     Why: A PDF is for reading; a template is a start for your own file.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/window-tour.html" poster="sims/window-tour.png" title="Window Tour: the parts of an Office app" >}}

3. In **Window Tour**, do the tasks of Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Which
   parts do the three apps share?

   {{< record "The three apps share …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The **title bar** with the file name, the **ribbon** under it and the
   **status bar** at the bottom. Only the work area is different: a page,
   a grid of cells or a slide.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which app makes each thing? Sort them.

   Word
   :   a document: pages of text

       Why: Word is the word processor.

   Excel
   :   a workbook with worksheets

       Why: Excel files are workbooks; each one has worksheets.

   :   the cell B3: column B, row 3

       Why: Cells are the boxes of an Excel worksheet.

   PowerPoint
   :   a presentation with slides

       Why: PowerPoint makes the slides of a talk.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Commands on the ribbon

**The idea:** the **ribbon** is the wide bar at the top of every Office app.
It has **tabs** (Home, Insert, Layout, Review). Each tab has **groups**
(Font, Paragraph), and each group has **commands** (Bold). Write the way
like this: **Home › Font › Bold**. Home has the common commands, Insert adds
things, Layout sets up the page. Save, Print and Share are on the **File**
tab.

**Aim:** find a command by its tab and its group, and write its way.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. In the notice, click in the title and find the command that puts it in
   the **center** of the line. Click it.

   {{< record "The way: Tab › Group › Command" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Home › Paragraph › Center**. The title moves to the middle of the
   line.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which way leads to **Center**?

   - [x] Home › Paragraph › Center

     Why: Center is a common command for a paragraph, so it is on the Home tab.

   - [ ] Insert › Paragraph › Center

     Why: The Insert tab adds things to a file.

   - [ ] Layout › Page Setup › Center

     Why: Page Setup is the setup of the whole page, not of one line.
   :::

2. At the end of the notice, press Enter and add a table of 2 columns and 3
   rows. Then turn the page to **Landscape**, and back to **Portrait**.

   {{< record "The way to Table … ; the way to Orientation …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Insert › Tables › Table** (move the mouse over the grid to 2 × 3,
   then click): you *add* a table, so it is on Insert. **Layout › Page
   Setup › Orientation**: the setup of the whole page is on Layout.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which tab has each command? Sort them.

   Home
   :   Center

       Why: A common command for text.

   :   Bold

       Why: Home › Font › Bold.

   Insert
   :   Table

       Why: You add a table.

   :   Pictures

       Why: You add a picture.

   Layout
   :   Orientation

       Why: Layout › Page Setup: the setup of the whole page.

   :   Margins

       Why: The margins belong to the whole page too.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/ribbon-finder.html" poster="sims/ribbon-finder.png" title="Ribbon Finder: tab, group, command" >}}

3. In **Ribbon Finder**, read each job and find its command on the ribbon.
   Where is the command for "Print the report"?

   {{< record "Print is on …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   On the **File** tab: **File › Print**. Commands for the whole file
   (Save, Print, Share, Export) are not on the ribbon tabs: they are on the
   File tab.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Ribbon Finder, where is the command for "Check the spelling of the
   report"?

   - [x] Review › Proofing › Spelling & Grammar

     Why: The Review tab checks a file: spelling, words and comments.

   - [ ] Home › Font › Spelling & Grammar

     Why: The Font group changes how the letters look.

   - [ ] File › Print

     Why: Print makes a paper copy; it does not check spelling.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · Save As, PDF and AutoSave

**The idea:** **Save** (Ctrl + S) puts the new changes in the same file.
**Save As** makes a **new copy** with a new name, a new place or a new
format; the old file stays. A **PDF** is for reading and printing: the look
stays the same on every computer, and nobody can change it easily.
**AutoSave** saves every change after a few seconds, but **only for files
in OneDrive**: for a file on the computer or a USB stick, press Ctrl + S
often.

**Aim:** keep your work safe, and make a copy that nobody can change.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word and File Explorer)**
:::

1. In the notice, click **File › Save As**. Choose the folder
   **Documents** and the name `2026-11-03_notice_v01` (use today's date).
   Click **Save**. Read the title bar.

   {{< record "The title bar now shows" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The new name, for example **2026-11-03_notice_v01**. Save As made a new
   copy. The start file `notice-start.docx` did not change.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   After **Save As**, what happened to `notice-start.docx`?

   - [x] Nothing: Save As made a new copy with the new name.

     Why: The title bar shows the new name; the start file did not change.

   - [ ] It got the new name.

     Why: The new name belongs to the new copy.

   - [ ] It was deleted.

     Why: Save As never deletes a file.
   :::

2. Click **File › Save As** again, change the type to **PDF** and click
   **Save**. Open the PDF and try to change one word.

   {{< record "The two files … ; can I change a word in the PDF?" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Two files with the same name: **2026-11-03_notice_v01.docx** (a Word
   document) and **2026-11-03_notice_v01.pdf** (a PDF). You **cannot**
   change a word in the PDF: it is for reading and printing. To change the
   notice, change the `.docx` file and save a new PDF.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   You cannot change a word in the PDF. To change the notice, put the steps in
   order.

   1. Open the `.docx` file in Word.
   2. Change the word.
   3. Save the `.docx` file.
   4. Save As PDF again.

   Why: A PDF is for reading and printing: change the Word file, then make a new PDF.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/save-lab.html" poster="sims/save-lab.png" title="Save Lab: Save, Save As and AutoSave" >}}

3. In **Save Lab**, do Tasks 1 to 3 (a power cut, then Save, then
   AutoSave in OneDrive). In which tasks is nothing lost? Record their numbers.

   {{< record "Nothing is lost in Tasks …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Tasks 2 and 3. Nothing is lost when you **saved before the power cut** (Task 2: only
   the sentence after Save is lost), or when **AutoSave is on for a file in
   OneDrive** (Task 3). In Task 1 the new sentence is lost.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   On a lab computer, the file is in Documents and AutoSave is **Off**. Why?

   - [x] AutoSave works only for files in OneDrive: press Ctrl + S often.

     Why: The file is on this computer, not in OneDrive.

   - [ ] The file is a PDF.

     Why: The file open in Word is the `.docx`.

   - [ ] Word saves only when you close it.

     Why: Word saves when you press Ctrl + S, or by itself with AutoSave in OneDrive.
   :::
